question.prompt:
How many nonnegative integers can be written in the form

\[ \begin{aligned} &a_7 \cdot 3^7 + a_6 \cdot 3^6 + a_5 \cdot 3^5 \\ &\quad {}+ a_4 \cdot 3^4 + a_3 \cdot 3^3 + a_2 \cdot 3^2 \\ &\quad {}+ a_1 \cdot 3^1 + a_0 \cdot 3^0, \end{aligned} \]

where \(a_i \in \{-1, 0, 1\}\) for \(0 \le i \le 7?\)

solutions.title: Shift the digits to base 3
solutions.explanation:
Adding \(1\) to each coefficient changes the allowed digits \(-1,0,1\) into the ordinary base-\(3\) digits \(0,1,2\). This lets us count distinct values without counting the same integer twice.

Write a represented integer as \(N=a_7 3^7+\cdots+a_0\), and let \(C=3^7+\cdots+3+1\). Then
\[
N+C=(a_7+1)3^7+\cdots+(a_1+1)3+(a_0+1).
\]
The right side is an eight-digit base-\(3\) representation, allowing leading zeros. Every such digit string is possible, and subtracting \(1\) from each digit recovers its coefficients. Uniqueness of ordinary base-\(3\) representation means different strings give different values of \(N+C\), and hence different values of \(N\).

There are three choices for each of the eight digits, so there are \(3^8=6561\) represented integers when negative values are included.

Zero is represented by taking all coefficients to be zero. Negating every coefficient changes \(N\) into \(-N\), so the nonzero represented values pair into one positive and one negative value. The number of nonnegative values is therefore
\[
1+\frac{6561-1}{2}=1+3280=3281.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{3281}\), choice \(\text{D}\).
